title: Indian Economy
summary: Planning legacy, national income, RBI and monetary policy, inflation indices, the Budget, taxes and GST, flagship schemes and economic institutions. CGL asks 2-3 questions, increasingly tilted to current numbers (rates, budget, index revisions).

subtopics.title: National income, growth and base years
subtopics.concept:
### National income concepts
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| GDP | Market value of all final goods & services produced **within India** in a year |
| GNP | GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFIA) |
| NNP | GNP − depreciation |
| Per capita income | NNP ÷ population |
| Factor cost vs market price | Market price = factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies |
| Nominal vs real GDP | Real GDP is at constant prices; **GDP deflator = (Nominal ÷ Real) × 100** |

### Bodies
- **NSO** (National Statistical Office, under **MoSPI**, formed 2019 by merging CSO + NSSO) estimates GDP and CPI-IIP series.
- **Economic Survey** — by the Department of Economic Affairs (Finance Ministry), released a day before the Budget.

### Base-year wave of 2026 (very exam-relevant)
| Indicator | Old base | New base | Release |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDP / National Accounts | 2011-12 | **2022-23** | 27 Feb 2026 (MoSPI) |
| CPI | 2012 | **2024** | 12 Feb 2026 (MoSPI) |
| IIP | 2011-12 | **2022-23** | effective 1 Jun 2026 (28-day lag) |
| WPI | 2011-12 | **2022-23** | 15 Jun 2026 (DPIIT); items raised **697 → 957**; Producer Price Indices (PPI) introduced — WPI to run alongside PPI for 5 years |

Economy sectors: primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing), tertiary (services). India is a **services-led** economy (over half of GVA).

formulas.name: NNP
formulas.note: GNP already includes net factor income from abroad

formulas.name: GDP deflator
formulas.note: divide nominal by (deflator/100) to get real

formulas.name: Market price bridge
formulas.note: moving between factor cost and market price

tricks.title: G-D-N ladder
tricks.body: GDP (territory) + NFIA = GNP; GNP − depreciation = NNP. 'Territory → Nation → Net'.

tricks.title: New base-year pairs
tricks.body: Production takes financial years: **GDP and IIP = 2022-23**; prices of consumers take a calendar year: **CPI = 2024**; wholesale moved to 2022-23 with PPI twins in June 2026.

mistakes: Calling GNP 'GDP minus NFIA' — it is GDP **plus** NFIA.
Quoting 2011-12 as the GDP base — since 27 Feb 2026 it is 2022-23.
Assuming the Economic Survey comes from MoSPI — it is a Finance Ministry (DEA) document.

subtopics.title: Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog
subtopics.concept:
### Five Year Plans (1951-2017)
| Plan | Period | Highlight / model |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | 1951-56 | Agriculture priority; based on Harrod-Domar model |
| 2nd | 1956-61 | **Mahalanobis model** — heavy industries |
| 3rd | 1961-66 | Self-reliance; wars and drought derailed it |
| Plan Holiday | 1966-69 | Three Annual Plans (after 1962/1965 wars) |
| 4th | 1969-74 | "Growth with stability"; 14 banks nationalised (1969) |
| 5th | 1974-79 | **Garibi Hatao**; terminated early |
| Rolling Plan | 1978-80 | Janata government concept (D.T. Lakdawala) |
| 6th | 1980-85 | Poverty removal focus; IRDP/NREP start |
| 7th | 1985-90 | Food, work, productivity |
| Annual Plans | 1990-92 | Transition years |
| 8th | 1992-97 | Ran against **LPG reforms** (1991 crisis) |
| 9th | 1997-2002 | "Growth with social justice" |
| 10th | 2002-07 | 8% target |
| 11th | 2007-12 | "Faster and more inclusive growth" |
| 12th (last) | 2012-17 | "Faster, more inclusive, sustainable growth" |

### NITI Aayog (since 1 January 2015)
Replaced the Planning Commission (set up 1950, Nehru). Created by a **Cabinet resolution** — neither constitutional nor statutory. PM chairs it; Governing Council of CMs/LG administrators; Vice-Chair **A.K. Lahiri** (since May 2026); CEO **Anurag Jain** (since Aug 2026). Works through a 15-year Vision, 7-year Strategy and 3-year Action Agenda; runs indices like the SDG India Index, Composite Water Management Index and Aspirational Districts Programme.

tricks.title: Plan-era story line
tricks.body: 1-farm (1951) → 2-machines (Mahalanobis) → 3-wars → holiday (66-69) → 4-stability + bank nationalisation → 5-Garibi Hatao → rolling (Janata) → 6-7 growth → 8-reforms (1992) → 9-12 inclusive → NITI (2015).

example.q: Which plan coincided with the LPG reforms?

tricks.title: Plan-break tags
tricks.body: Two gaps: **Plan Holiday 1966-69** (wars/drought) and **Annual Plans 1990-92** (transition after the 8th was delayed).

example.solution: 1962 and 1965 wars plus drought deranged the 3rd Plan; 1966-69 ran as annual plans.

mistakes: Saying NITI Aayog is statutory — it is a Cabinet-resolution body.
Crediting the 2nd Plan to Harrod-Domar — the 1st Plan's framework was Harrod-Domar; Mahalanobis belongs to the 2nd.
Assuming the 12th Plan ended early — it ran full term to 2017; NITI then took over.

subtopics.title: Money, banking and the RBI
subtopics.concept:
### Reserve Bank of India
Established **1 April 1935** under the **RBI Act, 1934** (Hilton Young Commission 1926); **nationalised 1 January 1949**; HQ **Mumbai**. Governor: **Sanjay Malhotra** (26th, since December 2024). Original capital shareholders included private hands until 1949; RBI is the currency issuer, banker to banks and to the government, and manages exchange reserves.

### Monetary Policy Committee (2016)
**6 members** (3 RBI incl. Governor with casting vote + 3 Government nominees); meets at least 4 times a year; mandate — CPI inflation **4% ± 2%**.

### Policy rates (after the 5 August 2026 MPC — held unchanged, neutral stance)
| Rate | Level | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Repo** | **5.25%** | Lending rate of RBI to banks (policy rate) |
| **SDF** | 5.00% | Floor; RBI borrows from banks at repo − 0.25% |
| **MSF / Bank Rate** | 5.50% | Ceiling; repo + 0.25% |
| **CRR** | **3.00%** | Cut from 4% in four 25-bp tranches (Sep–Nov 2025); earns banks nothing |
| **SLR** | 18% | Minimum share of deposits in gold/G-secs |
| Reverse repo | 3.35% | Dormant as operative rate since SDF's introduction (2022) |

Quantitative tools also include OMOs, USD/INR swaps, and VRR/VRRR auctions. **Cut CRR/repo → cheaper money → more liquidity; raise → inflation control.**

### Banking history
| Event | Year / fact |
|---|---|
| RBI set up | 1935; nationalised 1949 |
| SBI created (Imperial Bank → SBI) | **1955** |
| **14** banks nationalised (deposits ≥ ₹50 cr) | **19 July 1969** |
| **6** more banks (≥ ₹200 cr) | 15 April 1980 |
| RRBs started (Narasimham working group) | 1975 |
| Narasimham Committee I / II | 1991 / 1998 — banking-sector reforms, prudential norms |
| Nachiket Mor Committee | 2014 — financial inclusion, payments banks |

tricks.title: Corridor arithmetic
tricks.body: Repo is the middle: SDF = repo − 0.25 (floor), MSF = Bank Rate = repo + 0.25 (ceiling). With repo 5.25 → 5.00 / 5.25 / 5.50.

example.q: If repo were 6.00%, what would the MSF be?

tricks.title: Nationalisation anchors
tricks.body: 1935 born, 1949 nationalised (RBI), 1955 SBI, 1969 fourteen, 1975 RRBs, 1980 six.

example.q: How many banks in the 1980 round?

tricks.title: MPC fixed points
tricks.body: 6 members; 4 meetings a year minimum; target CPI 4% ± 2%; Governor's casting vote.

example.q: Who has the casting vote in the MPC?

mistakes: Repeating pre-2026 rates — repo is 5.25%, CRR 3%, not 6.5%/4%.
Confusing reverse repo (3.35%, dormant) with SDF (5.00%, the operative floor).
Crediting the Nachiket Mor committee with banking reforms of the 1990s — those were Narasimham I/II.

subtopics.title: Inflation and price indices
subtopics.concept:
### Inflation types
| Type | Cause |
|---|---|
| Demand-pull | Excess demand chasing goods |
| Cost-push | Rising input costs (oil, wages) |
| Stagflation | High inflation + stagnant growth + unemployment |
| Disinflation | Falling rate of inflation (still positive) |
| Deflation | Falling price level |
| Hyperinflation | Triple-digit monthly runaways |

### Measurement (post-2026 base revisions)
| Index | Compiler | Base | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CPI-Combined** (headline) | **NSO, MoSPI** | **2024** (new series from Feb 2026) | Rural + urban; anchors MPC's 4±2% target |
| **WPI** | Office of Economic Adviser, **DPIIT** | **2022-23** (from 15 Jun 2026) | Headline basket 957 items; excludes services; being replaced by PPIs over 5 years |
| IIP | NSO | 2022-23 (from 1 Jun 2026) | Monthly industrial output, 28-day lag |
| GDP deflator | NSO | ratio | Nominal/real GDP × 100 |

- **Core inflation** = headline CPI minus food and fuel.
- Inflation targeting framework: RBI Act amended **2016** (MPC), target **4% CPI ± 2%**, failure band defined as three consecutive quarters outside range.
- CPI food measure: **CFPI**; WPI fuel & power and manufactured products are the volatile groups; RBI uses CPI (not WPI) for policy.

tricks.title: Index-compiler pairs
tricks.body: CPI-IIP-GDP = MoSPI/NSO; WPI-PPI = DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser. 'M for MoSPI, W for DPIIT(OEA)'.

example.solution: Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Commerce & Industry Ministry).

tricks.title: Core = strip the volatile
tricks.body: Core inflation = headline − food − fuel. Stagflation = stagnation + inflation together.

example.q: If headline CPI is 6%, food & fuel contribute 2.5%, what is core?

mistakes: Using WPI for the inflation target — the MPC targets **CPI**.
Giving WPI the old 2011-12 base — since 15 June 2026 it is 2022-23 (957 items).
Calling disinflation 'deflation' — disinflation is only a slower rise, deflation is a fall.

subtopics.title: Budget and fiscal policy
subtopics.concept:
### Constitutional basis
- **Article 112** — Annual Financial Statement (the Budget); **Art. 266** Consolidated Fund; **Art. 267** Contingency Fund; **Art. 265** — no tax without authority of law.
- Railway Budget merged with the Union Budget in **2017**; presented on **1 February** since 2017. **Budget 2026-27** was presented by **Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026**.

### Budget 2026-27 at a glance (BE)
| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Total expenditure | ₹53.47 lakh crore (₹53,47,315 cr) |
| Total receipts (ex-borrowings) | ₹36.52 lakh crore; net tax receipts ₹28.7 lakh cr |
| Borrowings (fiscal deficit in ₹) | ₹16.96 lakh crore |
| **Fiscal deficit** | **4.3% of GDP** (RE 2025-26: 4.4%) |
| Revenue deficit | 1.5% of GDP |
| Primary deficit | 0.7% of GDP |
| Capital expenditure | **₹12.2 lakh crore** (from ₹11.2 lakh cr) |
| Central debt | 55.6% of GDP; glide path to ~50% by March 2031 |
| Disinvestment target | ₹80,000 crore |
| Nominal GDP growth assumed | 10% |

New in 2026-27: **Biopharma SHAKTI** (₹10,000 cr, 5 yrs), SME Growth Fund (₹10,000 cr), Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund, Semiconductor Mission 2.0, Electronics Component Manufacturing outlay raised to ₹40,000 cr, ₹20,000 cr carbon-capture allocation, City Economic Regions (₹5,000 cr each), MAT cut 15% → 14%.

### Deficit definitions
| Deficit | Formula |
|---|---|
| Fiscal | Total expenditure − total receipts **excluding borrowings** |
| Revenue | Revenue expenditure − revenue receipts |
| Primary | **Fiscal deficit − interest payments** |
| Effective capital expenditure | Capex + grants for creation of capital assets |

**FRBM Act, 2003** — fiscal discipline targets; amended periodically (current glide: fiscal deficit below 4.5% of GDP, then toward ~4%).

tricks.title: Budget 2026-27 number sheet
tricks.body: Spend 53.5 • Receipts 36.5 • Borrow 16.9 (₹ lakh crore); FD 4.3% • RD 1.5% • PD 0.7%; Capex 12.2; Debt 55.6%.

example.q: Which article is the Annual Financial Statement?

mistakes: Quoting 4.4% for FY27 — 4.4% is the 2025-26 RE; the BE 2026-27 is 4.3%.
Confusing primary deficit (fiscal − interest) with revenue deficit (revenue expenditure − receipts).
Thinking the railway budget still exists separately — merged in 2017.

subtopics.title: Taxation and GST
subtopics.concept:
### Direct vs indirect taxes
| Direct | Indirect |
|---|---|
| Income tax, corporate tax, capital gains, STT; burden cannot be shifted | GST, customs duty; burden shifted to consumer |

Direct-tax code change: the **Income-tax Act, 2025** replaces the 1961 Act **from 1 April 2026** — 536 sections in 23 chapters and a single **"tax year"** replacing assessment/previous year. Under the new regime (FY 2025-26 Budget), income up to ₹12 lakh attracts no tax (₹12.75 lakh for salaried with standard deduction).

### GST
- Introduced **1 July 2017** by the **101st Constitutional Amendment** — Articles **246A** (power to tax), **269A** (inter-state apportionment), **279A** (**GST Council**).
- **GST Council**: chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**; Union MoS Finance + State finance ministers; quorum = half; decisions by **3/4th weighted majority (Centre 1/3, States 2/3)**.
- **GST 2.0** (56th Council, 3 Sep 2025; effective **22 Sep 2025**): slabs collapsed to **5% and 18%**, plus a **40% demerit rate** for sin/luxury goods (12% and 28% abolished; compensation cess ended except pan masala & tobacco products). Small cars, ACs, TVs moved to 18%.
- GST compensation to States ran Jul 2017 – Jun 2022 under the Act.

### Other revenue markers
LTCG on equities 12.5% (> ₹1.25 lakh) since Budget 2024; STT raised in Budget 2026; buybacks taxed as capital gains for holders with promoter-level buyback tax. Customs is the only major indirect tax outside GST.

example.q: Which article created the GST Council?

tricks.title: GST 2.0 slab story
tricks.body: Two working slabs — 5 (merit) and 18 (standard) — with 40 kept aside for sin/luxury; 12% and 28% abolished on 22 Sep 2025.

example.q: GST on a small car now?

tricks.title: Tax-year switch
tricks.body: Income-tax Act, 2025 → effective 1 April 2026; one 'tax year' replaces previous/assessment year pair; 536 sections, 23 chapters.

example.q: From which income year does 'Tax Year' apply?

mistakes: Calling STT an indirect tax — it is a direct tax on transactions.
Assuming compensation cess continues on all goods — it ended 22 Sep 2025 except pan masala/tobacco lines.
Mixing the GST Council's 3/4 weighted majority with a 'simple majority of members'.

subtopics.title: Government schemes and missions
subtopics.concept:
### Flagship schemes (launch year — ministry — key fact)
| Scheme | Launch | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| PM Jan Dhan Yojana | 2014 | Financial inclusion; zero-balance accounts |
| Make in India / Skill India | 2014 | Manufacturing/employability push |
| **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** | 2015 | Women & child development + HRD + HUA (Panipat launch) |
| Atal Pension Yojana / Sukanya Samriddhi | 2015 | Pension for unorganised; girl-child savings |
| MUDRA Yojana | 2015 | Loans up to ₹10 lakh (Tarun Plus ₹20 lakh since Oct 2024) |
| PMAY (Urban) | 2015 | Housing for all |
| Ujjwala Yojana | 2016 | Free LPG connections to poor women |
| **PM-KISAN** | 2019 | ₹6,000/year to farmer families (Agriculture Ministry) |
| Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY | 2018 | ₹5 lakh/family health cover; **Vay Vandana** covers all 70+ (2024) |
| PM SVANidhi | 2020 | Working-capital loans for street vendors |
| PLI Schemes | 2020 | 14 sectors, production-linked incentives |
| PM Vishwakarma | 2023 | Support for 18 traditional trades |
| Namo Drone Didi / Lakhpati Didi | 2023 | Drones to women SHGs; ₹1 lakh+ annual income goal |
| PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli | 2024 | Rooftop solar; up to 300 free units/month |
| **VB-G RAM G** | **2025 Act, live 1 Jul 2026** | Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) — **replaces MGNREGA**; guarantee raised **100 → 125 days**; weekly wages |

### Budget 2026-27 additions
Biopharma SHAKTI (₹10,000 cr), Semiconductor Mission 2.0, Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund, SME Growth Fund (₹10,000 cr), City Economic Regions, five-part textile programme (incl. Samarth 2.0), Rare Earth corridors (Odisha, Kerala, AP, TN).

tricks.title: Launch-year clusters
tricks.body: 2014: Jan Dhan, Make in India • 2015: BBBP, APY, MUDRA, PMAY • 2016: Ujjwala • 2018: Ayushman • 2019: KISAN • 2020: SVANidhi, PLI • 2023: Vishwakarma, Drone Didi • 2024: Surya Ghar • 2026: VB-G RAM G live (125 days).

example.q: Which scheme gives ₹6,000 a year to farmers?

tricks.title: MGNREGA → RAM G swap
tricks.body: 100 → 125 days; 15-day → weekly wages; Act of 2025, in force 1 July 2026.

example.q: From when does VB-G RAM G apply?

mistakes: Attaching Ayushman Bharat to the Health Ministry alone — PM-JAY sits with Health, but BBBP is a three-ministry convergence.
Recalling MUDRA's ₹10 lakh limit but missing Tarun Plus (₹20 lakh, Oct 2024).
Believing MGNREGA still runs — it is replaced by VB-G RAM G from 1 July 2026.

subtopics.title: Regulators, exchanges and international organisations
subtopics.concept:
### Domestic regulators & institutions
| Body | Year | HQ | Head (2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| RBI | 1935 (nationalised 1949) | Mumbai | Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** |
| SEBI | 1988 (statutory 1992) | Mumbai | **Tuhin Kanta Pandey** (since Mar 2025) |
| IRDAI | 1999 (Act 2000) | Hyderabad | — |
| PFRDA | 2003 (Act 2013) | New Delhi | — |
| NABARD | **12 July 1982** | Mumbai | Refinances agriculture/rural credit (Shivaraman Committee) |
| SIDBI | 1990 | **Lucknow** | Refinances MSME credit |
| BSE | **1875 — Asia's oldest exchange** | Mumbai | SENSEX 30 stocks |
| NSE | 1992 (trading 1994) | Mumbai | NIFTY 50 stocks |

### International organisations (economy-facing)
| Org | Year | HQ | Chief (2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMF | 1944 (Bretton Woods) | Washington DC | MD **Kristalina Georgieva**; SDR quota reforms; reports: World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report |
| World Bank | 1944 (IBRD 1945) | Washington DC | President **Ajay Banga** (since Jun 2023); World Development Report |
| WTO | 1995 (succeeded GATT 1947) | Geneva | DG **Ngozi Okonjo-Iwealla**; India a founding member |
| ADB | 1966 | Manila | President Masato Kanda (2025) |
| AIIB | 2016 | **Beijing** | India a founding member (2nd largest shareholder) |
| NDB (BRICS) | 2015 | **Shanghai** | First president K.V. Kamath |
| OECD | 1961 | Paris | India is *not* a member |

tricks.title: Regulator HQ pairs
tricks.body: RBI-SEBI-NABARD = Mumbai; IRDAI = Hyderabad; SIDBI = Lucknow; PFRDA = New Delhi.

tricks.title: Bretton-Woods twins
tricks.body: IMF + World Bank both born at Bretton Woods (1944), both in Washington DC; WTO (1995, Geneva) replaced GATT (1947).

tricks.title: Asian banks map
tricks.body: ADB 1966 → Manila; AIIB 2016 → Beijing; NDB (BRICS) 2015 → Shanghai. India founding member in all three.

mistakes: Placing SEBI in New Delhi — it is Mumbai; PFRDA is the Delhi one.
Saying India is an OECD member — India is not (it engages as a Key Partner).
Assuming the IMF chief is always a European — tradition, not rule; Georgieva (Bulgarian) is the current MD.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The present repo rate / CRR / SDF is:'
pyqPatterns.approach: Memorise the corridor trio (5.00-5.25-5.50) plus CRR 3% and SLR 18%; refresh after every MPC.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The new CPI/WPI/GDP series uses which base year?'
pyqPatterns.approach: 2022-23 for GDP/IIP/WPI, 2024 for CPI; note compilers (NSO vs DPIIT).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The Second Plan was based on...' or 'Garibi Hatao belongs to which plan?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Story-line of 12 plans; anchor Mahalanobis-2nd, Harrod-Domar-1st, Garibi Hatao-5th, LPG-8th.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Fiscal deficit in Budget 2026-27 is...' or a small primary-deficit calculation.
pyqPatterns.approach: Know 4.3% (FY27 BE), ₹53.5 lakh crore spend; primary deficit = fiscal − interest.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'GST Council is chaired by...' / 'new slabs effective...'
Match pairs like PM-KISAN-Agriculture or the 125-day guarantee.
pyqPatterns.approach: Launch-year clusters table; note the 2025-26 swaps (VB-G RAM G, Vay Vandana).
Regulator HQ pairs + international bank HQs (Beijing AIIB, Shanghai NDB).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Consider the statements...' with one wrong absolute statement.
pyqPatterns.approach: Hunt for stale numbers (old rates, old base years) — that is usually the false one.

solvedExamples.q: If the nominal GDP of India is ₹300 lakh crore and the GDP deflator is 125, the real GDP (base-year prices) is:
solvedExamples.solution: GDP deflator = (Nominal ÷ Real) × 100, so Real = Nominal ÷ 1.25 = 300 ÷ 1.25 = **₹240 lakh crore**. Option (b) uses a wrong 133 deflator intuition; (c) multiplies instead of divides; (d) is a pure guess close to 240.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Deflator above 100 → divide nominal by (deflator/100) to get real.

solvedExamples.q: As per the RBI monetary policy of August 2026, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The SDF is 25 basis points below the repo rate
The MSF is 25 basis points below the repo rate
The Bank Rate is 40 basis points below the repo rate
The CRR stands at 4 per cent
solvedExamples.solution: Repo 5.25% → **SDF 5.00% (repo − 25 bp)**; MSF and Bank Rate are 5.50% (repo **+** 25 bp); CRR is **3%** (cut from 4% during Sep–Nov 2025). The corridor is SDF 5.00% — repo 5.25% — MSF 5.50%.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Corridor memory hook: SDF = repo minus a quarter, MSF = repo plus a quarter.

solvedExamples.q: From Budget 2026-27 figures — revenue receipts ₹35.3 lakh crore, revenue expenditure ₹41.3 lakh crore and interest payments ₹14.0 lakh crore — the revenue deficit is:
solvedExamples.solution: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts = 41.3 − 35.3 = **₹6.0 lakh crore** (actual RE figure ≈ ₹5.9 lakh crore, 1.5% of GDP). Option (a) is the primary deficit (16.9 − 14.0), (c) is the fiscal deficit, (d) is the previous year's RE.
solvedExamples.shortcut: First classify each number as revenue or fiscal — only revenue items enter revenue deficit.

solvedExamples.q: Under GST 2.0 (effective 22 September 2025), small cars and air-conditioners attract GST at:
solvedExamples.solution: The 56th GST Council's rationalisation moved most 28%-slab items — small cars, ACs, large TVs — to **18%**, while sin/luxury goods (pan masala, aerated drinks, luxury cars) went to the new **40%** demerit slab. The 12% slab was abolished altogether.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Ask 'sin or comfort?' — comfort items slid to 18%, sin items jumped to 40%.

practice.q: The Second Five Year Plan of India was based on which model of economic development?
practice.solution: The **2nd Plan (1956-61)** followed the **P.C. Mahalanobis model**, prioritising heavy and capital-goods industries. The 1st Plan leaned on the Harrod-Domar framework with an agriculture focus; the wage-goods critique came from Vakil-Brahmanand.
practice.shortcut: Second plan = heavy industry = Mahalanobis (the 'big machines' man).

practice.q: In which year were 14 major commercial banks nationalised in India?
practice.solution: **19 July 1969** — banks with deposits over ₹50 crore were nationalised; six more followed in April 1980 (₹200 crore threshold). SBI's creation from the Imperial Bank was in 1955, and the RBI itself was nationalised in 1949.

practice.q: With reference to NITI Aayog, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It was set up in 2014 as the successor to the Finance Commission
It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
It continues the Five Year Plan process
It was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission
practice.solution: NITI Aayog was created by a **Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission (1950) after the 12th Plan ended. It is neither constitutional nor statutory, and it does not allocate Plan funds.
practice.shortcut: Statutory test fails → only the '1 Jan 2015 replacement' statement can be true.

practice.q: The GST 2.0 rate rationalisation — with 5% and 18% slabs and a 40% demerit rate — took effect from:
practice.solution: The 56th GST Council **decided** the restructuring on 3 September 2025, but the new rates were **effective 22 September 2025** (first day of Navratri). 1 July 2017 is GST's launch date; 1 April 2026 is the Income-tax Act, 2025 date.
practice.shortcut: Decision 3 Sep, effect 22 Sep — decision first, delivery on Navratri.

practice.q: As per the RBI's monetary policy statement of August 2026, the policy (repo) rate stands at:
practice.solution: The MPC (5 Aug 2026) **unanimously held the repo at 5.25%** with a neutral stance — the rate last moved down through the 2025 easing cycle. 5.00% is the SDF floor and 5.50% the MSF/bank rate ceiling.
practice.shortcut: Remember the corridor trio 5.00–5.25–5.50; repo sits in the middle.

practice.q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is budgeted at what percentage of GDP?
practice.solution: **4.3% of GDP (BE 2026-27)**, improving on the 4.4% Revised Estimate of 2025-26; total expenditure is ₹53.47 lakh crore. The debt-to-GDP path heads from 55.6% toward about 50% by March 2031.

practice.q: The new series of the Consumer Price Index released in February 2026 uses which base year?
practice.solution: MoSPI's new CPI series (from 12 Feb 2026) shifts the base from **2012 to 2024**. 2022-23 is the new base for **GDP and IIP**, and the WPI moved to 2022-23 in June 2026.
practice.shortcut: Consumer prices anchor on a calendar year (2024); production series take financial years (2022-23).

practice.q: Which of the following constitutes M1 (narrow money) in India?
options: Currency with the public + time deposits with banks
Currency with the public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with the RBI
Currency with the public + post office savings deposits
practice.solution: **M1 = currency with the public + demand (current/savings) deposits with banks + 'other deposits' with the RBI.** Time deposits enter only M2/M3; post-office deposits sit outside M1, and M3 = M1 + time deposits (broad money).
practice.shortcut: Narrow = instantly spendable — currency plus demand deposits only.

practice.q: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA, guarantees:
options: 100 days of employment per household, as under MGNREGA
125 days of wage employment per rural household per year, effective 1 July 2026
practice.solution: The VB-G RAM G Act (2025) raises the statutory guarantee from 100 to **125 days** per rural household per financial year and came into force on **1 July 2026**, with weekly wage payments replacing the 15-day cycle.

practice.q: If a government's fiscal deficit is ₹12,00,000 crore and its interest payments are ₹9,00,000 crore, its primary deficit is:
practice.solution: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments = 12,00,000 − 9,00,000 = **₹3,00,000 crore**. Option (a) wrongly adds the two; (c) and (d) merely repeat given numbers.
practice.shortcut: Primary = fiscal minus interest — subtract, never add.

practice.q: India's new series of national accounts (GDP) released on 27 February 2026 has which base year?
practice.solution: MoSPI released the **GDP series with base year 2022-23** on 27 February 2026 (replacing 2011-12), with a far larger deflator set. IIP followed the same base from 1 June 2026; CPI uses calendar year 2024.
practice.shortcut: New GDP/IIP base = 2022-23; new CPI base = 2024.

practice.q: Which statement about the GST Council is correct?
options: It is chaired by the Prime Minister
States together carry one-third of the voting weight
Decisions require a two-thirds special majority of members present
Decisions are taken by a three-fourths weighted majority, with the Centre holding one-third weight
practice.solution: Under Art. 279A the Council is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, and every decision needs a **3/4th weighted majority — Centre 1/3, States together 2/3**; quorum is half the members.

practice.q: The revised Wholesale Price Index series released in June 2026 is characterised by:
options: inclusion of services in the headline WPI
an expanded basket of 957 items (from 697) alongside the launch of Producer Price Indices
a shift of compilation from DPIIT to NSO
practice.solution: DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser launched the WPI **2022-23 series on 15 June 2026**, expanding the basket from **697 to 957 items** and releasing new **Producer Price Indices**; WPI will run beside PPI for five years. Services remain outside headline WPI, and compilation stays with DPIIT.
practice.shortcut: Basket 697→957 and PPI twins — both changed together.

practice.q: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which becomes effective from 1 April 2026, is notable for:
options: introducing a single 'tax year' and replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961
raising the basic exemption limit to ₹7 lakh
practice.solution: The Income-tax Act, 2025 consolidates the 1961 Act into **536 sections across 23 chapters** and replaces the previous-year/assessment-year pair with one **'tax year'** (first applicable to income of FY 2026-27). Rates and slabs are essentially unchanged; GST law is untouched.
practice.shortcut: Keyword of the new Act = 'tax year' — nothing about GST or new slabs.

practice.q: Which one of the following is correct about India's Monetary Policy Committee and inflation target?
options: The MPC has 9 members and targets WPI inflation
The MPC has 6 members and targets CPI inflation of 4% with a ±2% band
The MPC has 6 members and targets CPI inflation of 5% with a ±1% band
The MPC has 4 members and the Governor has no casting vote
practice.solution: Since the RBI Act amendment of 2016, the **MPC has 6 members** (3 RBI including the Governor, who holds a casting vote, and 3 government nominees) with a flexible inflation target of **4% CPI ± 2%**.
